title: Synra plugin manifest
description: The manifest.json file at the root of a plugin package. It declares what the plugin is, which artifact implements it, and what it is allowed to do.

$schema.description: The URL of this schema. Editors use it for completion and validation.

schemaVersion.description: Manifest format version. Always 1 for this schema.

id.description: The complete scoped package id. Event ownership preserves this exact id, including publisher and conventional package prefixes.

title.description: Human-readable name, shown in the plugin list. Localizable via `locales`.

description.description: One or two sentences describing what the plugin does. Shown in the plugin list and in search results.

publisher.description: Who published this plugin. `id` and `pubkey` are bound together: the same id presenting a different key is treated as untrusted.

pubkey.description: Base64 ed25519 public key. Artifacts signed by the matching private key are accepted; a different key under the same `id` is not.

sdk.description: Which SDK versions this plugin can run against. The host refuses to activate a plugin whose minimum is above its own version.

max.description: Maximum SDK version, exclusive. Omit to allow any newer version.

wit.description: The WIT world version this plugin was built against, for example `synra:plugin@1.0.0`. A plugin built against an incompatible world is rejected at activation, before it runs.

runtime.description: What implements the plugin. `headless` is required; `ui` is optional and adds an interface. There is deliberately no `kind`, `isolation` or `target` field: those are deployment decisions made by the host, not properties of a plugin.

capabilities.description: Everything the plugin may do. The list is checked twice: at install time against the WIT imports the artifact actually references, and again on every call. A capability the user has not granted is refused even when it appears here.

shareHandlers.description: The kinds of shared content this plugin may be asked to handle. The host pre-filters on these before calling the plugin, so a plugin that does not list a kind is never woken for it.

description.description: Shown to the user when choosing between several plugins that can handle the same share.

actions.description: Named operations the plugin exposes. Other plugins and the plugin's own UI call these by name. The host rejects an invocation whose arguments do not match `args`.

name.description: Action name, unique within the plugin.

description.description: What the action does, shown in the UI and to other plugins.

args.description: JSON Schema for the arguments. Must be an object schema.

returns.description: JSON Schema for the return value.

events.description: Events this plugin emits. Each name must live under this plugin's own `_plugin.<full-plugin-id>.` namespace. Declaring them here is what lets the host check, at install time, that a paired device's copy of the plugin can still understand them.

name.description: Fully qualified event name, starting with `_plugin.<full-plugin-id>.`; the host checks that the owner equals this manifest's id.

payload.description: JSON Schema for the event payload. Must be an object schema with `additionalProperties: false`, and every `maxLength` or `maximum` must be bounded.

handles.description: Events this plugin wants to receive. An event that is not listed here is never delivered. Entries may name a built-in event or this plugin's own namespace; the host validates supported patterns.

event.description: An event name or a pattern with a trailing run of whole `*` segments, each matching one segment; for example `_plugin.@synra-plugin/chat.*`.

match.description: Extra conditions a payload must satisfy before the event is delivered. Keys are dotted paths into the payload.

compose.description: Other plugins this one builds on. The host activates dependencies first and refuses to activate this plugin if one is missing, unless the dependency is marked optional.

version.description: Semver range the dependency must satisfy, for example `^1.0.0`.

optional.description: When true, a missing dependency degrades the plugin instead of blocking activation.

network.description: Outbound hosts the plugin uses. This mirrors the `network:*` capabilities and exists so the interface can show a readable list at install time rather than a set of capability strings.

methods.description: Allowed HTTP methods. Omit to allow all.

pages.description: Interface pages this plugin provides. Requires `runtime.ui`.

key.description: Page identifier, unique within the plugin.

title.description: Page title shown in navigation and the window title.

path.description: Route for the page, relative to the plugin's namespace.

icon.description: Icon name from the built-in set.

resources.description: Resource limits the plugin would like. These are a request, not a guarantee: the host may tighten them according to how much the user trusts the plugin, and will never loosen them beyond its own ceiling.

preferredMemoryMb.description: Preferred linear-memory ceiling for the Wasm instance.

locales.description: Translated titles and descriptions. Keys are BCP 47 language tags. The host picks by the user's locale and falls back to the top-level `title` and `description`.

headlessRuntime.description: The Wasm component that implements the plugin's logic. It runs in the kernel's sandbox and is the only part of a plugin that can act on any device.

artifact.description: Path to the `.wasm` file, relative to the manifest. There is exactly one source for this path: both `synra-plugin verify` and the host's loader read this field.

maxMemoryMb.description: Memory ceiling the plugin requests for this artifact.

callTimeoutMs.description: Per-call time limit the plugin requests.

uiRuntime.description: The interface bundle. It is served from its own origin inside the host, so it can never reach the host's own pages or talk to the network directly.

artifact.description: Path to the `ui.zip` file, relative to the manifest.

entry.description: HTML entry point inside the zip, for example `index.html`.

defaultPage.description: `pages[].key` to open when the plugin's page is requested without one.

cap.description: A capability in `domain:resource:action` form. `*` matches one segment; `**` matches one or more.

optional.description: When true, the plugin still activates if this capability is not granted, and is expected to degrade. When false or absent, a missing grant blocks activation.

reason.description: Why the plugin needs this. Shown to the user in the permission prompt.
